podcast.body: A song released in September 1977, co-written with David Bowie, and used extensively to tell stories in various media, from movies to cars to beer commercials. It is the title track of Iggy's second solo album, which is considered his best work. "from September 1977, Iggy Pop with Lust for Life."

podcast.body: Released in 1977, this song is described as "ubiquitous" and has been a major source of income for Iggy Pop, notably through its use in commercials. Its drum beat was appropriated from the theme song of a nightly German news program, although the beats were considered so basic that exclusive ownership was difficult to claim. "The track dates back to 1977 when Iggy was cleaning up and drying out and detoxing in Berlin with his buddy David Bowie."

podcast.body: The title track from Iggy Pop's 1977 album, produced by David Bowie, became a rock radio staple. It gained further prominence as a favorite "movie and TV advert needle drop," ensuring that both Iggy Pop and the estate of David Bowie continue to receive payments when the song is used. "And Lust for Life, whose title track later became a rock radio staple and a favorite movie and TV advert needle drop."
